## Where the test actually runs

The Python file in GitHub defines the workload, but **GitHub is not the place where the production load is generated**. In the Azure setup, Azure Load Testing provisions a test engine and starts Locust on that engine. Locust then sends real HTTPS requests to `https://gimme-job.com`.

```diagram
Azure Load Testing engine → Locust virtual users → https://gimme-job.com → Cloudflare edge → Worker gimmejob → D1 gimmejob-db when needed → response → Azure/Locust statistics
```

This separates the **load generator** from the **system under test**:

- Azure Load Testing runs Locust and creates the virtual users.
- `gimme-job.com` is the target being measured.
- Cloudflare serves the requests and exposes server-side/runtime telemetry.
- The Worker `gimmejob` handles the application request.
- `GET /api/public/jobs` and `GET /api/dashboard` also exercise D1 `gimmejob-db`.
- A local Locust run changes only the load-generator location: Locust runs on the developer machine instead of an Azure engine.

The first Azure run used `LOCUST_TAGS=smoke`, so only the health task was eligible. The current workload also has a `public-read` selector. Setting `LOCUST_TAGS=public-read` makes Locust select among the four implemented non-health reads: `GET /`, `GET /reference/qa-fundamentals`, `GET /api/public/jobs`, and `GET /api/dashboard`. Route-specific selectors `home`, `reference`, `jobs`, and `dashboard` allow one path to be isolated.

## Where to read performance results

A useful performance test has **two views of the same run**. Azure/Locust shows what the load generator experienced; Cloudflare shows what happened inside the platform serving those requests.

| Question | Primary place to look |
| --- | --- |
| How many requests were sent and completed? | Azure Load Testing run dashboard |
| What were p50/p95/p99 response times? | Azure Load Testing statistics |
| What throughput/RPS did the test actually achieve? | Azure Load Testing |
| Which request failed or returned the wrong contract? | Azure/Locust errors and named-request statistics |
| Did the Worker hit runtime or CPU problems? | Cloudflare Workers metrics |
| Were there Worker exceptions or resource errors? | Cloudflare Workers metrics/logs |
| Did D1 queries become slower or scan more rows? | Cloudflare D1 analytics |
| What probably caused a latency increase? | Correlate Azure and Cloudflare over the same timestamps |

For GimmeJob, open the Azure Load Testing resource, select the test, then the concrete test run. That run is the source for client-side response time, throughput, request count and failure statistics.

In Cloudflare, use **Workers & Pages → gimmejob** for Worker metrics/Observability. Inspect request counts, invocation statuses/errors, CPU time, wall/execution time and logs/traces when needed. For D1-backed routes, also inspect the `gimmejob-db` analytics for read query rate, rows read and query latency.

The first health-only run can be understood mainly from Azure because its purpose was to validate the script and generated traffic. Once D1/public routes are exercised, Azure alone is not enough to diagnose a slowdown. Use Azure and Cloudflare together and align their graphs by the same test start/end timestamps.

Official references: [Azure Load Testing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-testing/load-testing/), [Cloudflare Workers metrics](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/metrics-and-analytics/), and [Cloudflare D1 metrics](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/observability/metrics-analytics/).

## Де фізично виконується тест

Python-файл у GitHub описує workload, але **GitHub не генерує production load**. У нашій Azure-конфігурації Azure Load Testing піднімає test engine і запускає на ньому Locust. Далі Locust надсилає реальні HTTPS requests до `https://gimme-job.com`.

```diagram
Azure Load Testing engine → Locust virtual users → https://gimme-job.com → Cloudflare edge → Worker gimmejob → D1 gimmejob-db за потреби → response → статистика Azure/Locust
```

Тут важливо розділяти **load generator** і **system under test**:

- Azure Load Testing запускає Locust і створює virtual users.
- `gimme-job.com` — target, який ми вимірюємо.
- Cloudflare обслуговує requests і дає server-side/runtime telemetry.
- Worker `gimmejob` обробляє application request.
- `GET /api/public/jobs` і `GET /api/dashboard` додатково навантажують D1 `gimmejob-db`.
- При local run змінюється лише місце load generator: Locust працює на developer machine, а не на Azure engine.

Перший Azure run мав `LOCUST_TAGS=smoke`, тому eligible був лише health task. У поточному workload також є selector `public-read`. Якщо задати `LOCUST_TAGS=public-read`, Locust вибиратиме між чотирма вже реалізованими non-health reads: `GET /`, `GET /reference/qa-fundamentals`, `GET /api/public/jobs` і `GET /api/dashboard`. Selectors `home`, `reference`, `jobs` і `dashboard` дозволяють ізолювати окремий route.

## Де дивитися результати performance test

Корисний performance test має **два погляди на той самий run**. Azure/Locust показує, що побачив load generator, а Cloudflare — що відбувалося всередині платформи, яка обслуговувала requests.

| Питання | Де дивитися насамперед |
| --- | --- |
| Скільки requests було відправлено і завершено? | Azure Load Testing run dashboard |
| Які були p50/p95/p99 response times? | Azure Load Testing statistics |
| Який throughput/RPS реально досягнуто? | Azure Load Testing |
| Який request упав або порушив contract? | Azure/Locust errors і named-request statistics |
| Чи Worker уперся у runtime або CPU limit? | Cloudflare Workers metrics |
| Чи були Worker exceptions/resource errors? | Cloudflare Workers metrics/logs |
| Чи D1 queries стали повільнішими або читали більше rows? | Cloudflare D1 analytics |
| Що, ймовірно, спричинило зростання latency? | Кореляція Azure і Cloudflare за однаковими timestamps |

Для GimmeJob в Azure відкрий Azure Load Testing resource, вибери test, а потім конкретний test run. Саме цей run є основним джерелом client-side response time, throughput, request count і failure statistics.

У Cloudflare відкрий **Workers & Pages → gimmejob** і дивись Worker Metrics/Observability: request count, invocation statuses/errors, CPU time, wall/execution time, а за потреби logs/traces. Для D1-backed routes додатково дивись analytics `gimmejob-db`: read query rate, rows read і query latency.

Перший health-only run можна було зрозуміти переважно з Azure, бо його метою була перевірка script і generated traffic. Коли тестуємо D1/public routes, одного Azure вже недостатньо для діагностики slowdown. Azure і Cloudflare треба дивитися разом, вирівнюючи графіки за однаковими start/end timestamps тесту.

Офіційні джерела: [Azure Load Testing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-testing/load-testing/), [Cloudflare Workers metrics](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/metrics-and-analytics/) і [Cloudflare D1 metrics](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/observability/metrics-analytics/).
